summary: Intermittent RBAC role removal after Okta group sync causing 403s to internal Feature Flags console
summary_short: Users intermittently lose RBAC roles after Okta sync; some see 403s to Feature Flags console
description:
Issue summary:
Intermittent removal of RBAC roles for employees after scheduled Okta group synchronization. Affected users lose access to the internal Feature Flags console and other RBAC-protected endpoints and receive 403 responses. Problem appears after periodic full-group syncs and is sometimes resolved by re-login but recurs for a subset of identities.

Impact:
Multiple internal engineers (SRE and Product) blocked from feature flagging flows during deployment windows; impact is production and preventing emergency toggles. Approximately 12 unique users reported in first wave.

Environment:
Production (us-west) identity sync pipeline: Okta -> SCIM provisioner -> identity-service role-mapper -> console. Scheduled full-group sync runs nightly 03:00 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Wait for scheduled full Okta group sync (nightly or manual trigger)
2) Have a user who is member of multiple Okta groups with overlapping role mappings (e.g., engineering-team + deployers) log into Console
3) Observe that the identity-service issues a 200 for token exchange but the console returns 403 for RBAC-protected routes
4) Re-login/SSO often restores access intermittently; in some cases a manual forced SCIM resync recovers roles for a user
5) Users with single, simple group mappings are not affected in observed cases
logs_and_traces: Splunk: search index=auth sourcetype=scim_provisioner status=500 "group-attribute-mapper" | earliest=-6h | stats count by error_code
Console error example: 2026-03-09T03:02:20Z - 403 - role "deployers" not found for principal sub=U12345
investigation_notes: 03/09 04:10 - Initial triage: observed correlation between nightly full sync start and first error reports (3 users).
03/09 05:00 - Replayed sync in staging and hit attribute-mapper 502s when group list length > 120; suspect batching bug.
03/09 07:20 - Identity-service logs show role claim normalization step dropped duplicate group names but did not merge aliases (alias groups with same display name across different org units).
Hypothesis: race between SCIM provisioner and role-mapper cache invalidation where group aliasing causes transient drop of role claim until the next sync or token refresh.
Observed partial failure pattern: SCIM returned HTTP 202 for some group updates while sync coordinator marked job successful; downstream role reconciler did not process partial updates correctly.
Related: linked issue INT-462199 describes a cookie stripping redirect loop that previously masked token refreshs — could explain why some users need a full browser restart to recover.
Temporary mitigation tested: manual SCIM resync + clearing identity-service group cache for affected principals restores access consistently.
PR opened to add stricter idempotency checks and backoff on scim-provisioner: github.com/redwood-inference/scim-provisioner/pull/197 (in review).
comments: 2026-03-09T05:12 - Marco Liu: Assigned to me for initial SRE triage. Confirmed 3 reports, pulling logs and queue sizes.
2026-03-09T06:02 - Priya Desai (Auth Eng): Noted recent deploy of group-alias normalization (identity-service v1.9.2). Rolling back to v1.9.1 eliminated failures in a staging replay.
2026-03-09T07:35 - Marco Liu: Manual resync and cache purge performed for 12 affected users; all confirmed recovered. Created follow-up tasks for automation.
2026-03-10T09:10 - SRE Lead (Jon Erickson): Requesting a hotfix to add defensive handling for partial SCIM responses and a stricter sync success criterion.
2026-03-10T14:40 - QA (Elena Gomez): Running expanded staging test with >200 group memberships per principal to validate batching edgecases.
2026-03-11T11:22 - Marco Liu: Hotfix PR prepared for identity-service to fail sync on partial commit and to force reconciliation run post-sync: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-service/pull/482
resolution: Mitigation performed: manual SCIM resync and identity-service cache purge restored access for all reported users. Hotfix PRs opened: identity-service #482 (adds fail-on-partial-sync + immediate reconciliation), scim-provisioner #197 (idempotency and backoff). Scheduled emergency deploy of hotfix to production 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC with rollback plan. Follow-ups: add end-to-end sync tests, increase monitoring thresholds for partial syncs, document manual cache purge runbook.
follow_up_tasks: Create automated end-to-end test that replays large group merges (>200 groups) - owner: QA
Add a reconciliation step post-sync that verifies role claims across services - owner: Auth Eng
Implement alerting for partial-successful SCIM jobs with >1% failure rate - owner: SRE
Document manual cache purge and resync runbook in Confluence and link from identity-service runbook
